title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: vignette covers conditional row formatting ksTFL: compute_cols() six action functions — c_style(), c_merge(), c_addrow(), c_glue(), c_clear(), c_pageBreak(). Rules declared data applied render; post-processing pass needed.

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Prerequisites: complete Getting Started basic compute_cols() familiarity. focus row-level logic, helper functions, composable actions stay readable rules grow.

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Apply style references cells based conditions: Result: response cell shows green bold text CR rows red bold text PD rows; columns untouched:
code: library(ksTFL)  data <- data.frame(   patient = sprintf("PAT-%03d", 1:20),   age = c(23, 45, 67, 34, 89, 56, 42, 71, 38, 29,           55, 66, 44, 52, 60, 48, 35, 70, 41, 58),   response = sample(c("CR", "PR", "SD", "PD"), 20, replace = TRUE) )  # Define styles first spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "highlight_green", s_font(color = "#006400", bold = TRUE)) |>   add_style(id = "highlight_red", s_font(color = "#8B0000", bold = TRUE))  # Apply conditional styling spec <- spec |>   compute_cols(     response == "CR",     c_style(response, styleRef = "highlight_green")   ) |>   compute_cols(     response == "PD",     c_style(response, styleRef = "highlight_red")   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Merge multiple columns single display cell: Result: consecutive rows group, group visit cells merge one display cell showing group value. merged cell keeps text leftmost column merged range (report column order), regardless order columns listed cols; columns’ values shown. Note: cols argument c_merge() must resolve least two consecutive columns final report column order. Overlapping merges allowed: second one dropped warning.
code: data_groups <- data.frame(   group = c("Treatment A", "Treatment A", "Treatment A",             "Placebo", "Placebo"),   visit = c("Week 0", "Week 4", "Week 8", "Week 0", "Week 4"),   value = c(5.2, 6.1, 7.3, 4.8, 5.5) )  spec <- create_table(data_groups) |>   compute_cols(     !firstOf(group),  # not the first row of each run of this group value     c_merge(c(group, visit))   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Insert new rows based data patterns: Result: inserted row one full-width cell: empty text without value_from, styled styleRef — style reads band section header. copy single column’s value inserted row use value_from (see later examples). Use pos = "" insert matching row instead.
code: spec <- create_table(data_groups) |>   compute_cols(     firstOf(group),  # First row of each group     c_addrow(pos = "above")  # Insert an empty separator/header row above   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Insert page break matching row. useful force new page logical grouping large block ends. Result: renderer start new page rows matching condition. break ends current table segment next segment repeats column-header row. match first data row changes nothing — row already starts page.
code: spec <- create_table(data_groups) |>   compute_cols(     firstOf(group),  # Insert page break starting from first row of each group     c_pageBreak()   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Conditions actions evaluated spec$.metadata$data_env, contains: Data columns: Direct access columns (even invisible ones) Helper functions: firstOf(), lastOf(), firstRow(), lastRow(), rowNumber(), everyNth(), firstOfBlock() Embedded functions: Internal utilities column access Important: helper functions available inside cond argument compute_cols(). standalone exported functions — call outside compute_cols(). Style references passed actions can also name built-atoms (b, , ar, indent_1, bg_mint, bt_th, …; full catalog via tfl_print_style_atoms() Styling Guide); f_combine() merges several atoms one reference.
code: # You can reference any column directly in conditions spec <- create_table(data) |>   compute_cols(     age > 60 & response %in% c("CR", "PR"),  # Multi-column condition     c_style(c(age, response), styleRef = f_combine('b', 'bg_mint'))   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: following helpers available exclusively inside compute_cols() conditions: firstOf(...): Logical vector TRUE first row RUN equal values specified columns (run-length semantics). Sort data upstream logical group contiguous — value re-appears later starts new run matches . lastOf(...): , TRUE last row run. firstRow(): Logical vector TRUE first row lastRow(): Logical vector TRUE last row rowNumber(): Integer vector row numbers (1-based) everyNth(n): Logical vector TRUE every nth row starting row 1 (everyNth(2) marks odd rows 1, 3, 5, …; use rowNumber() %% 2 == 0 even rows) firstOfBlock(col, n = 1, offset = 0): TRUE first row every n-th RUN col values, excluding first run — n = 1 marks start runs 2, 3, 4, …; n = 2 marks runs 3, 5, … sort precondition firstOf().
code: # Highlight first and last rows using helper functions spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "border_emphasis",             s_font(bold = TRUE),             s_table_style(borders = s_borders(top = s_border(width = "2pt"),                                               bottom = s_border(width = "2pt")))) |>   compute_cols(     firstRow() | lastRow(),     c_style(everything(), styleRef = "border_emphasis")   )  # Use firstOf/lastOf for value-based boundaries spec <- create_table(data_groups) |>   add_style(id = "group_boundary", s_font(bold = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(     firstOf(group) | lastOf(group),     c_style(group, styleRef = "group_boundary")   )  # Use everyNth for alternating patterns spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "gray_bg", s_table_style(background_color = "#F5F5F5")) |>   compute_cols(     everyNth(2),  # marks odd rows: 1, 3, 5, ...     c_style(everything(), styleRef = "gray_bg")   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Use tidyselect style multiple columns :
code: data_lab <- data.frame(   patient = sprintf("PAT-%03d", 1:10),   hemoglobin = rnorm(10, 13.5, 1.5),   glucose = rnorm(10, 95, 15),   cholesterol = rnorm(10, 200, 30) )  spec <- create_table(data_lab) |>   add_style(id = "out_of_range", s_font(color = "#FF4500", bold = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(     hemoglobin < 12 | hemoglobin > 16,     c_style(hemoglobin, styleRef = "out_of_range")   ) |>   compute_cols(     glucose < 70 | glucose > 140,     c_style(glucose, styleRef = "out_of_range")   ) |>   compute_cols(     cholesterol > 240,     c_style(cholesterol, styleRef = "out_of_range")   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Merge across multiple grouping levels:
code: data_nested <- data.frame(   study = rep(c("Study A", "Study B"), each = 6),   phase = rep(c("Phase I", "Phase II", "Phase III"), 4),   site = rep(c("Site 1", "Site 2", "Site 1", "Site 2"), 3),   enrollment = sample(10:50, 12) )  spec <- create_table(data_nested) |>   # Merge study column for consecutive same-study rows   compute_cols(     !firstOf(study),     c_merge(c(study, phase, site))   ) |>   # Merge phase column within same study   compute_cols(     !firstOf(study, phase),     c_merge(c(phase, site))   )

text: Combine merging conditional styles:
code: spec <- create_table(data_nested) |>   add_style(id = "merged_header",             s_font(bold = TRUE),             s_table_style(background_color = "#E0E0E0")) |>   compute_cols(     !firstOf(study),     c_merge(c(study, phase, site))   ) |>   compute_cols(     firstOf(study),  # First row of group     c_style(study, styleRef = "merged_header")   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Insert calculated summary rows:
code: data_sales <- data.frame(   region = c("North", "North", "South", "South", "West", "West"),   product = rep(c("A", "B"), 3),   revenue = c(100, 150, 200, 120, 180, 160),   total =   c(250, 250, 320, 320, 340, 340) )  spec <- create_table(data_sales) |>   add_style(id = "summary_row",             s_font(bold = TRUE),             s_table_style(background_color = "#D3D3D3")) |>   # we do not need the `total` column itself - set to invisible   define_cols(total, isVisible = F) |>    compute_cols(     lastOf(region),  # Last row of each region     # Insert subtotal row     c_addrow(pos = "below",               value_from = total, #value from total column              styleRef = f_combine("summary_row", 'ar'))     )

text: Insert section (group) headers make stub: complex example two-level indents: result getting two-level stub:
code:
data_sales <- data.frame( region = c("North", "North", "South", "South", "West", "West"), product = rep(c("Gas", "Oil"), 3), revenue = c(100, 150, 200, 120, 180, 160) ) spec <- create_table(data_sales) |> # Custom style just for fun add_style(id = "section_header", s_font(bold = TRUE, font_size = "10pt", color = '#FFFFFF'), s_table_style(background_color = "#4682B4")) |> # Hide the `region` column as we want to use its value as heading define_cols(region, isVisible = F) |> # Add column labels: define_cols( c(product, revenue), label = c('Region
Product', 'Revenue
(Million of $)'), # Use embedded indent style to indent the `product` value in a column valueStyleRef = c('indent_1', NA) # NA here means we are not using any style for `revenue` ) |> # Use `c_addrow` to add a line with the value from `region` column compute_cols( firstOf(region), # First row of each new region c_addrow(pos = "above", value_from = region, styleRef = "section_header") ) data_sales <- data.frame( region = c("North", "North", "North", "South", "South", "South", "West", "West", "West"), product = rep(c("Total","Gas", "Oil"), 3), revenue = c(250, 100, 150, 320, 200, 120, 340, 180, 160) ) spec <- create_table(data_sales) |> # Hide the `region` column as we want to use its value as heading define_cols(region, isVisible = F) |> # Add column labels: define_cols( c(product, revenue), label = c('Region
Product', 'Revenue
(Million of $)') ) |> # Use `c_addrow` to add a line with the value from `region` column compute_cols( firstOf(region), # First row of each new region c_addrow(pos = "above", value_from = region, styleRef = 'b') ) |> # the `Total` value will be indented 0.5cm compute_cols( product == 'Total', c_style(product, f_combine('i', 'indent_1')), c_style(revenue, 'i') ) |> # Other values ('Gas', 'Oil') will be indented by 1cm compute_cols( product != 'Total', c_style(product, 'indent_2') )

what: c_glue(): Append or Prepend Text to Cell Values
title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: c_glue() concatenates literal string data column value display text matching cells — useful appending units, prefixing markers, building composite labels without creating extra columns. Parameters: cols: columns modify (tidyselect) position: "" "" — attach text glue_col: unquoted name data column whose value attach text: literal string (single value) attach separator: string inserted original value glued text (default "") Provide exactly one glue_col / text. appear compute_cols() call, parser warns keeps glue_col, ignoring text. Glue lands raw cell text: cell suppressed dedupe merged non-leader renders blank glued part skipped — target merge leader. cols must match visible report columns; glue_col may reference hidden one. c_glue() fully compatible c_style() c_merge() compute_cols() call.
code: data_units <- data.frame(   parameter = c("Hemoglobin", "Glucose", "Cholesterol"),   value     = c(13.5,          95.0,      200.0),   unit      = c("g/dL",        "mg/dL",   "mg/dL") )  spec <- create_table(data_units) |>   # Hide the unit column — use it only as a glue source   define_cols(unit, isVisible = FALSE) |>   # Append unit to value: "13.5" → "13.5 g/dL"   compute_cols(     !is.na(value),     c_glue(value, position = "after", glue_col = unit, separator = " ")   )

what: c_clear(): Blank Cell Content in Matching Rows
title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: c_clear() renders specified cells empty (blank) matching rows without removing column affecting layout. Useful conditional deduplication, dedupe parameter define_cols() enough. Note: c_clear() affects rendered display text. underlying data value still available conditions compute_cols() calls. Actions run arrival order, c_clear() c_glue() call turns glue full cell replacement, c_glue() c_clear() erases glued result.
code: data_groups <- data.frame(   group  = c("Treatment A", "Treatment A", "Treatment A", "Placebo", "Placebo"),   visit  = c("Week 0", "Week 4", "Week 8", "Week 0", "Week 4"),   value  = c(5.2, 6.1, 7.3, 4.8, 5.5) )  spec <- create_table(data_groups) |>   # Show group label only on first row of each group; blank it on the rest   compute_cols(     !firstOf(group),     c_clear(group)   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Chain multiple compute_cols() calls c_* actions build fully formatted table: can see simple planar data frame: become production ready table:
code:
data_sales <- data.frame( region = c("North", "North", "North", "South", "South", "South", "West", "West", "West"), product = rep(c("Oil", "Gas", "TOTAL"), 3), revenue = c(100, 150, 250, 200, 120, 320, 180, 160, 340) ) spec <- create_table(data_sales) |> add_style(id = "section_header", s_font(bold = TRUE, font_size = "11pt", color = '#FFFFFF'), s_table_style(background_color = "#4682B4")) |> # Make Region invisible, since we want to make it as header row define_cols(region, isVisible = F) |> # Define column labels define_cols(c(product, revenue), label = c('Product', 'Revenue
(Million of $)')) |> # Make a header row from the `region` value compute_cols( firstOf(region), # First row of each new region c_addrow(pos = "above", value_from = region, styleRef = "section_header") ) |> # Create a summary row for `Total` value # Note here how a consecutive calls to `c_*` atomic functions produce final result compute_cols( product == 'TOTAL', # merge `product` and `revenue` to a single column (the value became value from `product`) c_merge(c(product, revenue), styleRef = f_combine('b','i','bt_th','ar')), # clear the value, since we want to rebuild it: c_clear(product), # take the value of `region` into the merged cell... c_glue(product, 'after', glue_col = region), # then the word 'total: ' ... c_glue(product, 'after', text = ' total: '), # and finally the `revenue` value to complete the string c_glue(product, 'after', glue_col = revenue) )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Every compute_cols() block adds one condition/action group spec one resolution pass create_report(). case_when construct inside conditions — group rules shared condition apply together, keep style lookups cheap reusing ids:
code: # Three rules over the same column (idiomatic): spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "young",  s_font(color = "#008000")) |>   add_style(id = "middle", s_font(color = "#0000FF")) |>   add_style(id = "senior", s_font(color = "#FF0000")) |>   compute_cols(age < 30, c_style(age, styleRef = "young")) |>   compute_cols(age >= 30 & age < 60, c_style(age, styleRef = "middle")) |>   compute_cols(age >= 60, c_style(age, styleRef = "senior"))  # When the same action set applies to several ranges, merge the ranges # into ONE condition with `|`: spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "extreme", s_font(bold = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(age < 25 | age >= 65, c_style(age, styleRef = "extreme"))

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Avoid row--row operations custom functions:
code: # ❌ Slower (scalar logic): spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "responder", s_font(bold = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(     sapply(response, function(x) x %in% c("CR", "PR")),  # Row-by-row     c_style(response, styleRef = "responder")   )  # ✅ Faster (vectorized): spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "responder", s_font(bold = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(     response %in% c("CR", "PR"),  # Vectorized     c_style(response, styleRef = "responder")   )

what: 3. Tighten Conditions, Do Not Split Tables
title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: Conditions evaluated vectorized, one pass per block whole columns — per-row cost optimize. rows need styling, make condition selective (e.g. age > 80), data: split one logical table across two specs formatting reasons, spec becomes Word table report.

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: ksTFL automatically consolidates identical styles, can help reusing style references:
code: # ✅ Define once, use many times: spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "critical", s_font(color = "#FF0000", bold = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(age > 80, c_style(age, styleRef = "critical")) |>   compute_cols(response == "PD", c_style(response, styleRef = "critical"))  # ❌ Avoid duplicate style definitions: # (This creates two identical but separate styles) spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "critical_age",      s_font(color = "#FF0000", bold = TRUE)) |>   add_style(id = "critical_response", s_font(color = "#FF0000", bold = TRUE))

code: # The analyst frame carries a pre-computed per-region total in `total` # (same value repeated on every row of the region). data_totals <- data.frame(   region  = rep(c("North", "South"), each = 2),   product = rep(c("A", "B"), 2),   revenue = c(100, 150, 200, 120),   total   = c(250, 250, 320, 320) )  spec <- create_table(data_totals) |>   add_style(id = "total_row",             s_font(bold = TRUE),             s_table_style(background_color = "#FFD700")) |>   define_cols(total, isVisible = FALSE) |>   compute_cols(     lastOf(region),  # Last row of each region     # copy the region total into a full-width row below it     c_addrow(pos = "below", value_from = total, styleRef = "total_row")   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: condition expression must evaluate logical vector exactly one element per data row, single logical scalar (recycled rows). Anything else errors create_report(): Scalar-returning aggregates work — recycled across rows: Still, recommended idiom precomputing helper columns upstream — explicit, cacheable, lets invisible columns drive several rules :
code: # ❌ Wrong-length result: the condition may capture fine, but #    create_report() aborts because it resolves lazily: spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "above_average", s_font(italic = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(     age > head(mean(age), 0),  # returns logical(0), not one value per row     c_style(age, styleRef = "above_average")   ) create_report(spec)  # aborts: condition must return a length-20 logical spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "above_average", s_font(italic = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(     age > mean(age),   # scalar mean -> age > 29.5 for every row     c_style(age, styleRef = "above_average")   ) data$age_above_avg <- data$age > mean(data$age)  spec <- create_table(data) |>   define_cols(age_above_avg, isVisible = FALSE) |>   compute_cols(     age_above_avg,     c_style(age, styleRef = "above_average")   )

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: can’t nest action functions: Workaround: Use separate compute_cols() calls:
code: # ❌ This is invalid: actions are siblings, not expressions that can be #    nested inside each other's arguments. (Aborts at create_report(): #    the nested c_merge() has no compute_cols() context when resolved.) spec <- create_table(data) |>   compute_cols(     age > 60,     c_style(age, styleRef = c_merge(c(patient, age)))  # Not allowed   ) create_report(spec) spec <- create_table(data) |>   compute_cols(age > 60, c_style(age, styleRef = "elderly")) |>   compute_cols(age > 60, c_merge(c(patient, age)))

title: Advanced StyleRows and Conditional Formatting in ksTFL
text: styleRef must reference previously defined style: Workaround: Always define styles using :
code: # ❌ This will error at evaluation time (create_report validates all #    referenced style ids): spec <- create_table(data) |>   compute_cols(age > 60, c_style(age, styleRef = "undefined_style")) create_report(spec) spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "elderly", s_font(bold = TRUE)) |>  # Define first   compute_cols(age > 60, c_style(age, styleRef = "elderly"))

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: ksTFL partitions table columns four categories determine widths calculated: Displayed report output Participate width calculations default state columns Maintain exact specified width (unit: %, cm, ) Fixed automatic recalculation Can use relative (%) absolute (cm, ) units Automatically recalculated fill available space Normalized proportionally based initial auto-detected weights visible unlocked columns participate recalculation Hidden output completely Automatically assigned width “0.0cm” Excluded width calculations Data still accessible conditional logic (e.g., compute_cols())

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: create table, ksTFL automatically: Analyzes column’s data type content Estimates visual width widest rendered cell (numeric values measured auto-guessed %d / %.df format), longest line column name, label — whichever longest. Frames 10,000 rows deterministically sampled measurement. Distributes widths proportionally sum 100% Clamps column 5%–60% band, renormalizes 100%, rounds one decimal drift correction (largest column absorbs rounding remainder)
code: library(ksTFL)  # Create sample data data <- data.frame(   id = 1:100,   patient_id = sprintf("PAT-%04d", 1:100),   age = round(rnorm(100, 45, 10)),   weight_kg = round(rnorm(100, 70, 15), 1),   treatment_group = sample(c("Placebo", "Treatment A", "Treatment B"), 100, replace = TRUE) )  # Initial spec with auto-detected widths spec <- create_table(data) print(spec)  # Shows auto-calculated widths for all columns

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: autoColWidth option (default: TRUE) controls whether widths automatically recalculated lock column change column’s visibility:
code: # Check current setting print(tfl_get_option("autoColWidth"))  # TRUE by default  # Disable for manual width management tfl_set_options(autoColWidth = FALSE)  # Re-enable (restore default behavior) tfl_set_options(autoColWidth = TRUE)

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: set colWidth column, becomes LOCKED:
code: # Lock the 'id' column at 15% spec <- create_table(data) |>   define_cols(id, colWidth = "15%")  # Result: # - id: 15% (LOCKED) # - Other visible columns: auto-recalculated to fill remaining 85%

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: can lock multiple columns; unlocked columns fill remaining space: Flag columns (isPaging, isGrouping, isColBreak) recalculate like unlocked column — lock widths size matters. column-break segments, ID columns keep width remaining segment columns rescaled fill segment.
code: spec <- create_table(data) |>   define_cols(id, colWidth = "10%") |>           # Lock at 10%   define_cols(patient_id, colWidth = "20%") |>   # Lock at 20%   define_cols(treatment_group, colWidth = "25%") # Lock at 25%  # Result: # - id: 10% (LOCKED) # - patient_id: 20% (LOCKED) # - treatment_group: 25% (LOCKED) # - age, weight_kg: share remaining 45% proportionally

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: autoColWidth = TRUE lock column, ksTFL: Partitions columns LOCKED UNLOCKED Calculates available space: 100% minus sum locked percentage widths Normalizes unlocked widths fill available space proportionally Rounds 1 decimal place drift correction

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: sample data (100 rows), create_table() measures content produces distribution: Note content-aware initial split : narrow numeric id age columns keep 7.5%, long text column treatment_group takes 37.5%.
code: # Initial auto-distribution (measured for this dataset): # id: 7.5%, patient_id: 25.0%, age: 7.5%, weight_kg: 22.5%, treatment_group: 37.5%  spec <- create_table(data) |>   define_cols(id, colWidth = "10%")    # After locking id at 10%: # - Available space: 100% - 10% = 90% # - Unlocked weights: patient_id=25.0, age=7.5, weight_kg=22.5, treatment_group=37.5 (sum=92.5) # - Normalized into 90%: patient_id=24.3%, age=7.3%, weight_kg=21.9%, treatment_group=36.5% # - Total is exactly 100.0% after drift correction

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: ensure widths sum exactly 100%, ksTFL applies drift correction: Rounds widths 1 decimal place Calculates total rounding error (drift) Adds/subtracts drift largest unlocked column sum exact; largest unlocked column absorbs correction.

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: Use isVisible = FALSE hide columns output:
code: spec <- create_table(data) |>   define_cols(id, isVisible = FALSE)  # Result: # - id: hidden, width = "0.0cm" (automatic) # - Other columns: recalculated to fill 100%

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: set colWidth invisible columns: ? Invisible columns always “0.0cm”—setting width contradictory.
code: # This will error: spec <- create_table(data) |>   define_cols(id, isVisible = FALSE, colWidth = "15%")    # Error message (verbatim): # Cannot set `colWidth` for invisible column "id" # x Column "id" has `isVisible = FALSE` # i Invisible columns automatically have `colWidth = "0.0cm"`

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: Invisible columns exist mainly : driving conditional formatting.
code: spec <- create_table(data) |>   add_style(id = "highlight_yellow",             s_font(bold = TRUE),             s_table_style(background_color = "#FFFF99")) |>   # Define/lock widths BEFORE hiding (invisible columns reject colWidth)   define_cols(patient_id, isVisible = FALSE) |>   # Use the hidden column in compute_cols() for conditional styling   compute_cols(     startsWith(patient_id, "PAT-001"),     c_style(age, styleRef = "highlight_yellow")   )

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: complete manual control:
code: # Disable auto-recalculation tfl_set_options(autoColWidth = FALSE)  # Set exact widths - no automatic adjustment spec <- create_table(data) |>   define_cols(     c(id, patient_id, age, weight_kg, treatment_group),     colWidth = c("10%", "25%", "20%", "20%", "25%")   )  # Widths stay exactly as specified (sum = 100%)  # Re-enable for other tables tfl_set_options(autoColWidth = TRUE)

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: Precision: need exact widths without rounding Complex layouts: Multi-level headers specific alignments Pre-calculated: ’ve determined optimal widths externally

what: Width Floors and the Unlocked Reserve
title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: Two different constants apply widths: Relative widths (%) set : minimum 0.5% Absolute widths (cm, ) set : minimum 0.2cm (~0.08in) minColWidth (default 0.5%): space validator reserves column stays UNLOCKED lock another one floor width type fixed 0.5% — minColWidth lower . minColWidth controls space check .
code: # This will error: spec <- create_table(data) |>   define_cols(id, colWidth = "0.1%")  # Below the fixed 0.5% floor    # Error message (verbatim): # Column width "0.1%" is below minimum allowed # x Relative widths must be at least 0.5% # i Proposed: 0.1%

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: ksTFL prevents locking widths leave insufficient space columns stay unlocked: Rule thumb: column stays unlocked, locked relative widths must sum 99.5% — validator keeps minColWidth reserve last unlocked column, error names exact allowed maximum.
code: # 5 columns, minColWidth = 0.5% (default): # the 4 unlocked columns need 4 x 0.5% = 2% of the space.  # This will error: spec <- create_table(data) |>   define_cols(id, colWidth = "99%")  # Leaves only 1% for 4 columns    # Error message (verbatim): # Cannot set column `id` to "99%" # x This would leave insufficient space for the remaining 4 unlocked #   columns to meet the minimum width of 0.5%. # i After this change, 4 columns need 2% total. Remaining space available: 1%. # i Maximum allowed relative width for `id`: 98.0% # i Reduce the proposed width or adjust other locked widths

title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: Raise lower per-unlocked-column reserve trade strictness layout freedom:
code: # A 12-column frame: locking one column at 95% would leave 5% for 11 # unlocked columns, each needing 0.5% (5.5% total) — rejected. wide_data <- as.data.frame(replicate(12, sample(100:999, 10))) names(wide_data) <- paste0("COL", 1:12)  tfl_set_options(minColWidth = 0.5) spec <- create_table(wide_data) |>   define_cols(COL1, colWidth = "95%")  # errors: max allowed is 94.5%  # Relax the reserve and the same lock goes through: tfl_set_options(minColWidth = 0.3) spec <- create_table(wide_data) |>   define_cols(COL1, colWidth = "95%")  # OK  tfl_set_options(minColWidth = 0.5)  # restore default

what: Issue: A width shifts by more than a tenth of a percent after recalculation
title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: Cause: Drift correction. largest unlocked column absorbs whole rounding correction total stays exactly 100%; many unlocked columns correction can exceed 0.1% one column. Solution: expected handled automatically. rendered output correct.

what: Issue: Can’t set width for invisible column
title: Column Width Management in ksTFL
text: Cause: Trying use colWidth isVisible = FALSE Solution: Remove colWidth argument — invisible column rendered “0.0cm” takes space, width meaningless.

what: Issue: Widths change unexpectedly after define_cols()
title: Column Width Management in ksTFL

what: 1. Why does cols not drop the other columns from my data?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: cols presentation lens, data-mutation step. ksTFL keeps full input data inside spec’s shadow data later compute_cols() calls can still reference helper fields never appear document. One caveat: cols still defines table’s column set. Conditions can reference excluded fields, define_cols(), c_style(), c_merge(), c_clear() c_addrow(value_from = ...) accept columns selected — excluded column can tested, never styled. helper columns prefer keeping cols hiding isVisible = FALSE (see question 2).

what: 2. Can I hide a column and still use it in compute_cols()?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Yes. standard helper-column pattern: set isVisible = FALSE keep using column conditions value_from arguments. Hiding keeps column spec’s column set — label, styleRef, value_from conditions still work ; width removed. Excluding via create_table(cols = ...) stronger operation: actions reject column (see question 1). package examples hide fields SECTION, SECTION_ID, MODELVAL, SOC_GROUP.
code: spec <- create_table(df) |>   add_style("flagged", s_font(color = "#8B0000", bold = TRUE)) |>   define_cols(FLAG, isVisible = FALSE) |>   compute_cols(FLAG == "Y", c_style(c(PARAM, VALUE), styleRef = "flagged"))

what: 3. Why can I not set colWidth on an invisible column?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Invisible columns forced width "0.0cm" removed width recalculation entirely. column must reserve visual space, truly invisible stay visible.

what: 4. Why did the other column widths change after I locked one column?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Setting colWidth locks columns. autoColWidth = TRUE (default), ksTFL re-normalizes remaining visible unlocked columns fill leftover width. call, ID stays fixed 20% remaining visible unlocked columns recalculated fill rest. Two hard constraints come locking: locked widths must leave least 0.5% last unlocked column (sum locks <= 99.5%), width set 0.5% relative (0.2 cm absolute) floor — define_cols() errors name maximum allowed exceed budget.
code: spec <- create_table(df) |>   define_cols(ID, colWidth = "20%")   # ID locked; rest re-normalized

what: 5. Why did c_glue() not modify a repeated value?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: renderer paints raw cell, dedupe = TRUE cell suppressed paint time — glue landing deliberately shown. skip happens non-leader cells inside merge: glue leader column, drop dedupe field let repeated values show.

what: 6. Can I use aggregate logic such as mean(x) inside a compute_cols() condition?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Yes scalar-returning aggregates: conditions evaluated whole column vector, age > mean(age) works (scalar mean recycled row-wise). allowed anything changes vector shape — subsetting like head(x), summaries grouped per row, returning wrong length: condition must yield one logical per row (single scalar) — never NA. condition yields NA errors render, guard comparisons !.na(x). Still, section-level statistics recommended pattern precomputing helper column upstream — keeps rules explicit reusable.
code: df$group_mean <- ave(df$AVAL, df$GROUP, FUN = mean)  spec <- create_table(df) |>   add_style("flagged", s_font(bold = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(group_mean > 10, c_style(AVAL, styleRef = "flagged"))

what: 7. Can I nest c_*() actions inside each other?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: . Row actions siblings, nested verbs. Caveat c_addrow() headers: later compute_cols() block c_clear() c_glue() matching header’s source rows also hit inserted row (shares source cell); later c_style() repaint . clear rule must spare header, exclude source rows block’s condition. Either pass multiple actions one compute_cols() call use several compute_cols() calls condition.

what: 8. Why does every add_span_header() call create a new row of headers?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: stubOrder auto-increments omit . Reuse stubOrder sibling span headers belong one header row, increase really want new level. Higher stubOrder renders higher page; stubOrder = 1 sits directly column-label row. Auto-increment therefore stacks new call top previous bands — set stubOrder explicitly whenever visual level matters.
code: spec <- create_table(df) |>   add_span_header(c(TRT_A_N, TRT_A_PCT), label = "Treatment A", stubOrder = 1) |>   add_span_header(c(TRT_B_N, TRT_B_PCT), label = "Treatment B", stubOrder = 1) # same stubOrder = same header row; columns must not overlap within a row

title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Yes across different levels, within one. Bands stubOrder must use disjoint column sets — overlap hard error. Bands different levels may cover columns; covered column’s label merges row lowest band .

what: 10. How do I keep a small table under a figure on the same page?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Set continuousSection = TRUE following spec, first one. Keep page size margins compatible across sections, use pattern short follow-content Word still handles overflow naturally.
code: report <- create_report(   create_figure(plot_obj),              # a ggplot object or an image path   create_table(summary_tbl) |>     set_document(continuousSection = TRUE)   # the FOLLOWING spec gets joined ) write_doc(report, name = "fig_with_table", outDir = "output",           metaPath = "meta")

what: 11. When should I use isGrouping, isPaging, and isColBreak?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Use isGrouping value change defines logical section, isPaging value change start new vertical page group, isColBreak wide listing split horizontally segments repeating ID columns.

what: 12. Why do my footnotes repeat on every page?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: default: footnotePlace = "repeated". Switch "last_page" want final note block , "doc_footer" note belongs Word footer area. option applies specs created call; change one existing table, set spec: set_document(footnotePlace = "last_page"). doc_footer released binaries 0.12.0, pair footnote least one add_footer() — builds drop note footer part exists. Current master auto-creates footer part.
code: tfl_set_options(footnotePlace = "last_page")

what: 13. Why does firstOf() mark more rows than I expected?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: firstOf()/lastOf() (firstOfBlock()) work contiguous runs, unique values — run-length encoding. column like GROUP = , B, , firstOf(GROUP) TRUE three rows: starts new run. ksTFL never re-sorts rows; arrange() input grouping columns create_table(), helpers simply mark run boundaries meant.
code: df <- df[order(df$GROUP), ]   # make each group contiguous spec <- create_table(df) |>   compute_cols(firstOf(GROUP), c_addrow(pos = "above", value_from = GROUP))

what: 14. What is the practical difference between write_doc(),
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: save_report(), replay_report()? write_doc() one-step path everyday use. save_report() writes spec JSON plus table/figure payloads without rendering, replay_report() renders later saved artifacts can also combine previously saved outputs one document. write_doc appends .docx name (pass “tables”, “tables.docx”); save_report stores docFileName verbatim — include extension replay--document-name lookups match.
code: # one step write_doc(report, name = "tables")  # two steps saved <- save_report(report, docFileName = "tables.docx", metaPath = "meta") # NOTE: save_report() itself does NOT render a DOCX — it only writes the # spec/data JSON into metaPath. replay_report() (or write_doc) renders. replay_report(saved$spec_file, meta_dir = "meta")

what: 15. When do I need a persistent metaPath instead of tempdir()?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Use tempdir() need final DOCX right now. Use persistent metaPath want exact replays, QC comparison, report inventories, later combined replay workflow. replay DOCX name, ksTFL resolves latest saved spec meta folder; need exact historical version, replay saved JSON file name instead. Relative outDir/metaPath/meta_dir strings resolve working directory — non-interactive runs pass normalizePath() absolute paths set output_directory/meta_directory options.
code: replay_report("tables.docx", meta_dir = "meta") replay_report("abc123def456.json", meta_dir = "meta")

what: 16. Can I delete the original figure file after saving a report?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: replay-based workflows, yes successful save, ksTFL copies figure metaPath dataRef. saved meta folder becomes durable rendering input. copy happens inside save_report()/write_doc() — call succeeds spec still points original file (ggplot exports live session tempdir). Delete source files successful save.

what: 17. Why did different sections of one report use different templates?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: default behavior multi-spec reports. spec resolves docTemplate, table can use one bundled template text figure section uses another.
code: report <- create_report(   create_table(adsl) |> set_page_style(docTemplate = "Navy_Pro"),   create_text()      |> set_page_style(docTemplate = "Carbon_Dark") ) write_doc(report, name = "mixed_sections", outDir = "output", metaPath = "meta")

what: 18. How do I force one template across every section?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Use overrideTemplate write_doc() replay_report(). global override wins per-spec docTemplate values cleanest way re-skin finished bundle.
code: write_doc(report, name = "tables", outDir = "output", metaPath = "meta",           overrideTemplate = "Navy_Pro") replay_report("tables.docx", meta_dir = "meta", overrideTemplate = "Navy_Pro")

what: 19. Why does a Table of Contents not appear even though I asked for one?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: need parts contract: request TOC (toc = TRUE, insertTOC = TRUE, package option) mark least one title subtitle toclevel. TOC request toclevel entries nothing index.
code: spec <- create_table(df) |>   add_title("Table 1", toclevel = 1)  write_doc(create_report(spec), name = "tables", outDir = "output",           metaPath = "meta", toc = TRUE) # In Word: click the TOC field and press F9 to populate it.

what: 20. Why is the TOC still just a placeholder when I open the DOCX?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: ksTFL writes Word TOC field, pre-expanded static table. Open file Word, click inside TOC, update fields F9 populate .

what: 21. Can create_report() accept a named list of specs built in a loop?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Yes. create_report() accepts named lists TFL_spec objects, useful specs created dynamically separate program files. list names become key prefixes inside final TFL_report.
code: specs <- list(   demog = create_table(adsl),   labs  = create_table(adlb) )  report <- create_report(specs)   # slot names become key prefixes names(report) # "demog_<hash>" "labs_<hash>"

what: 22. How do I define several display columns in one place?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Use one define_cols() call columns share labels, widths, base value styles. keeps aligned numeric columns easy maintain.
code:
spec <- create_table(adsl) |> define_cols( c(AGE, WEIGHT, HEIGHT), label = c("Age", "Weight
(kg)", "Height
(cm)"), colWidth = c("12%", "14%", "14%"), valueStyleRef = c("ar", "ar", "ar") ) # Locked widths must leave >= 0.5% for the last unlocked column; the # remaining visible columns share what is left (autoColWidth) — see the # Column Width Management vignette.

what: 23. How do I use NA to skip one column inside a batch define_cols() call?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Use NA position want leave unchanged. handy columns share one update one column keep existing definition. column hidden call rejects non-NA colWidth (error names column) — keep hide final call, stub-header recipe . AGE keeps current label width, TRT01A keeps current value style. also works well hidden helper columns want skip colWidth invisible columns forced "0.0cm".
code: spec <- create_table(adsl) |>   define_cols(     c(USUBJID, AGE, TRT01A),     label = c("Subject ID", NA, "Treatment"),     colWidth = c("18%", NA, "20%"),     valueStyleRef = c("font_courier_new", "ar", NA)   )

what: 24. How do I hide a helper column but still use it to drive formatting?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Hide helper isVisible = FALSE, refer compute_cols() usual. standard pattern QC flags, section ids, hidden totals.
code: spec <- create_table(df) |>   add_style("flagged", s_font(color = "#8B0000", bold = TRUE)) |>   define_cols(c(PARAM, VALUE), label = c("Parameter", "Value")) |>   # hide last: invisible columns reject colWidth and are excluded from recalc   define_cols(FLAG, isVisible = FALSE) |>   compute_cols(     FLAG == "Y",     c_style(c(PARAM, VALUE), styleRef = "flagged")   )

what: 25. How do I turn a hidden grouping column into a stub header?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Use c_addrow() first row group pull display text hidden column. usually cleaner repeating region every detail row.
code: spec <- create_table(df) |>   add_style(     "section_header",     s_font(bold = TRUE, color = "#FFFFFF"),     s_table_style(background_color = "#4682B4")   ) |>   # labels/widths first, hide LAST (invisible columns reject colWidth):   define_cols(c(PRODUCT, REVENUE), label = c("Product", "Revenue")) |>   define_cols(REGION, isVisible = FALSE) |>   compute_cols(     firstOf(REGION),     c_addrow(       pos = "above",       value_from = REGION,       styleRef = "section_header"     )   )

what: 26. How do I insert subtotals from a hidden total column?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Precompute subtotal upstream, hide helper column, insert last row group. works well display row just formatted version stored summary text.
code: spec <- create_table(df) |>   add_style(     "subtotal_row",     s_font(bold = TRUE),     s_table_style(background_color = "#D9D9D9")   ) |>   # labels/widths first, hide LAST (invisible columns reject colWidth):   define_cols(c(PRODUCT, REVENUE), label = c("Product", "Revenue")) |>   define_cols(TOTAL, isVisible = FALSE) |>   compute_cols(     lastOf(REGION),     c_addrow(       pos = "below",       value_from = TOTAL,       styleRef = f_combine("subtotal_row", "ar")     )   )

what: 27. How do I apply one condition to several visible columns at once?
title: FAQ and Practical Gotchas in ksTFL
text: Pass column vector c_style() instead repeating condition separate calls. Use flag belongs row columns show .
code: spec <- create_table(labs) |>   add_style("out_of_range", s_font(color = "#FF4500", bold = TRUE)) |>   compute_cols(     VISIT == "Week 8" & AVAL > AVAL_ULN,     c_style(c(PARAM, AVAL, UNIT), styleRef = "out_of_range")   )

what: 28. How do I combine font and background styles for one rule?

code: # From a file path — PNG, JPEG/JPG, or SVG (the renderer's supported formats) png_plot <- file.path(tempdir(), "plot.png") png(png_plot, width = 600, height = 400) plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg); dev.off() spec_fig <- create_figure(png_plot)  # From a ggplot2 object — rendered automatically to a temporary image file. # The DEFAULT device is "cairo": a paths-only SVG (text converted to vector # outlines), which is the MS Word-safe vector format. library(ggplot2) p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point() spec_fig <- create_figure(p)             # cairo SVG (default) spec_fig <- create_figure(p, dpi = 150L) # dpi applies to raster devices only  # Device options: #   figureDevice = "cairo" (default) -> Word-safe paths-only SVG (needs Cairo) #   figureDevice = "svg"             -> svglite text-SVG: renders correctly in #                                        LibreOffice but is CROPPED/RESKINNED #                                        by MS Word (font substitution, #                                        text-anchor, px-scaling bugs) — #                                        use only when Word is not the target #   figureDevice = "png"/"jpeg"      -> raster (300 dpi by default) # If Cairo/svglite are missing, ksTFL falls back cairo -> svg -> png with a # one-time warning, so figure production never breaks on a dev machine. # # Two sizing knobs: session options figureWidth/figureHeight set the EXPORT # size for ggplot objects at create_figure() time; set_document(figureWidth = # ..., figureHeight = ...) sizes only the box the image is embedded into. # tfl_set_options(figureWidth = "8in", figureHeight = "5in", figureDevice = "png") # # The default scale mode "fixed" stretches whatever you embed into the # width/height box. To keep a file figure's own aspect ratio, use # set_document(figureScaleMode = "fitKeepAR") — it reads the intrinsic AR of # the PNG/JPEG/SVG and fits it into the body area.

title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: Key parameters: label: Column header text type: “numeric” “string” (auto-detected omitted) format: Format string (e.g., “%.2f”, “0.00”) colWidth: Column width string unit "%", "", "cm" (e.g. "20%", "2cm"). set, column locked width unlocked columns auto-recalculate sum 100%. Locked widths must leave least 0.5% last unlocked column (total locked <= 99.5%). Disable auto-recalculation tfl_set_options(autoColWidth = FALSE). isVisible: TRUE (default) FALSE. hidden column renders width “0.0cm”, excluded width recalculation, rejects colWidth set call — set labels/widths first, hide last. isID: TRUE column repeats page breaks dedupe: TRUE clear consecutive repeating values column isColBreak: TRUE column needs moved next page (break long tables) labelStyleRef: Style(s) apply column header valueStyleRef: Style(s) apply cell values Hiding Columns: See Reporting Examples detailed column customization patterns.
code: # Different format for each column spec <- define_cols(spec, c(mpg, cyl, hp),   label = c("MPG", "Cylinders", "HP"),   type = c("numeric", "numeric", "numeric"),   format = c("%.1f", "%.0f", "%.0f")) dat <- data.frame(group_id = 1:3, value = c(1.5, 2.5, 3.5)) spec <- create_table(dat) |>   define_cols(group_id, isVisible = FALSE) # Result: group_id is hidden, other columns recalculated to fill 100%

title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: Create reusable named styles add_style(): Best practice: Define styles , reference id (name) throughout spec. style needs used across many tables define thru tfl_set_options() make available session-wide. comprehensive styling details see Styling Guide.
code: spec <- create_table(mtcars)  # Header style: bold, 12pt, centered, gray background spec <- add_style(spec, id = "table_header",   s_font(font_name = "Arial", font_size = "12pt", bold = TRUE),   s_paragraph(alignment = "center"),   s_table_style(background_color = "#E0E0E0"))  # Numeric style: right-aligned spec <- add_style(spec, id = "numeric_right",   s_paragraph(alignment = "right"))  # Apply to columns spec <- define_cols(spec, c(mpg, hp),   labelStyleRef = "table_header",   valueStyleRef = "numeric_right")

title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: Create multi-level headers add_span_header() using tidyselect expressions: Tidyselect support: add_span_header() accepts tidyselect expressions: Key concepts: cols: Column names span. Names resolve full data frame, intersect spec’s columns, column excluded via create_table(cols = ...) silently selects nothing. Accepts: Unquoted names: c(mpg, cyl, hp) Quoted names: c("mpg", "cyl", "hp") Ranges: mpg:hp Helpers: starts_with("c"), contains("w"), matches("^m") Negation: -mpg (columns except mpg) label: Spanning header text stubOrder: Vertical stacking order — HIGHER numbers render HIGHER page. stubOrder = 1 band directly column-label row, stubOrder = 2 sits (0 negatives allowed — every band still renders column labels; sort value). Auto-generated NULL: later call takes next number stacks earlier ones — builds staircase, one band per call. Prefer explicit stubOrder every call: sibling bands belong row share number (column sets must overlap). labelStyleRef: style id defined via add_style(), style atoms combined f_combine() (see Styling Guide), band label. Rules: Stubs stubOrder share columns (prevents ambiguous headers) Stubs different stubOrder values can overlap freely (enables hierarchical structure) Multiple stubs order allowed long column sets don’t overlap Use add_style() style stub labels use embedded atomic styles See Styling Guide styling stubs.
code: spec <- create_table(mtcars) spec <- define_cols(spec, c(mpg, cyl, hp, wt),   label = c("MPG", "Cyl", "HP", "Weight"))  # Band 1 (directly above the column-label row): finer grouping — these two # share one row because their column sets do not overlap spec <- add_span_header(spec, cols = c(mpg, cyl, hp),   label = "Engine",   stubOrder = 1) |> add_span_header(cols = wt,   label = "Weight",   stubOrder = 1) |> # Band 2 (higher on the page): full-width banner above both add_span_header(cols = c(mpg, cyl, hp, wt),   label = "Motor Vehicle Specs",   stubOrder = 2) # Fresh spec (stub sets must not overlap within one stubOrder) spec_ts <- create_table(mtcars)  # Using column ranges and helpers spec_ts <- add_span_header(spec_ts, cols = mpg:hp, label = "Engine block", stubOrder = 0) |>   add_span_header(cols = wt:qsec, label = "Chassis", stubOrder = 0)

what: Step 5: Add titles, footnotes, headers, footers
title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: Add document content layers: Notes: add_header() add_footer() take 3 separate string arguments: left, center, right Placeholders like {PAGE} {NUMPAGES} filled renderer Multiple add_header() calls append additional header rows; use level parameter replace specific row Multiple add_footnote() calls stack order add_title() add_subtitle() accept optional toclevel parameter (integer, 1 9). set, title included Table Contents generated write_doc(toc = TRUE). TOC Word field: entries written render, Word populates list field updates (F9, print preview). add_title()/add_subtitle() CALL contributes one entry — multi-line vector title stays single entry.
code: spec <- create_table(mtcars)  # Titles and subtitles spec <- add_title(spec, "Motor Trend Car Road Tests") spec <- add_subtitle(spec, "Analysis of 1974 road-test data")  # Footnotes (document-level notes) spec <- add_footnote(spec, "Values are from 1974 Motor Trend magazine.")  # Page headers (left/center/right) — three separate string arguments spec <- add_header(spec, "Study ABC", "CONFIDENTIAL", "Page {PAGE}")  # Page footers (left/center/right) — three separate string arguments spec <- add_footer(spec, "Company", "Locked DB", "2025")  # Body text (narrative) spec <- add_body_text(spec, "This analysis includes all subjects in the safety population.")

title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: Use set_page_style() p_page() p_margins() control physical page layout: p_page() parameters: size: Page size — "A4" (default), "A3", "Letter", "Legal", "Executive". orientation: "portrait" "landscape". omitted, TEMPLATE’s orientation applies — every bundled template except Classic_portrait landscape, bare p_page(size = "A4") still comes landscape. margins: margins object p_margins(). margin fields accept dimension strings ("1in", "2.54cm", "72pt", "25.4mm"). p_margins() parameters (accept dimension strings like "1in", "2.54cm", "72pt", "25.4mm"): top, bottom, left, right: Page margins header, footer: Distance page edge header/footer content
code: spec <- create_table(mtcars) |>   set_page_style(     page = p_page(       size        = "A4",        # "A4", "A3", "Letter", "Legal", "Executive"       orientation = "landscape",  # "portrait" or "landscape"       margins     = p_margins(         top    = "1in",         bottom = "1in",         left   = "0.75in",         right  = "0.75in",         header = "0.5in",         footer = "0.5in"       )     )   )

title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: Templates control visual appearance (colours, fonts, borders) rendered DOCX: Bundled templates: Default, Navy_Pro, Carbon_Dark, Classic_portrait, Classic_landscape_times, Listings, Regulatory_Arial (confirm time tfl_list_templates()). Use docTemplate spec different sections one report keep different looks. Use write_doc(..., overrideTemplate = ...) replay_report(..., overrideTemplate = ...) want one global template override every spec rendered document. Use run_styles_editor() interactively create edit template JSON files.
code: # List all bundled templates tfl_list_templates()  # Apply a bundled template spec <- create_table(mtcars) |>   set_page_style(docTemplate = "Navy_Pro")  # Or apply via set_document() spec <- create_table(mtcars) |>   set_document(hasData = TRUE, docTemplate = "Carbon_Dark")  # Use a custom external template (JSON file). An ABSOLUTE path always works. A # RELATIVE path is checked against your working directory at authoring time and # stored verbatim; at render time it is resolved against the render working # directory first and, when not found there, against the directory of the saved # spec JSON (and its parent) — so replaying a saved report from another folder # still finds a template that sits next to the saved spec. Only when every # candidate misses does the package warn and fall back to the "Default" # template. For portable scripts, keep the template next to the saved spec # (the meta folder), where replay can always resolve it, or use a bundled # name. At authoring time the relative path must already exist in the # working directory — set_page_style() errors if it does not. (Any template JSON works, including a copy of a bundled # one, which is what this example does.) my_tpl <- file.path(tempdir(), "my_custom_template.json") file.copy(system.file("templates", "Navy_Pro.json", package = "ksTFL"), my_tpl) spec <- create_table(mtcars) |>   set_page_style(docTemplate = my_tpl)

title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: Beyond global column styling, apply conditional actions specific rows match condition: Common use cases: Highlight group headers: style first/last row group run Add separators: insert empty rows groups Merge columns: create group headers merging adjacent columns Conditional formatting: style rows meeting threshold (e.g. value > 100) Key action functions (used inside compute_cols()): Condition syntax: Key concepts: Conditions evaluated , create_report() finalizes spec — call compute_cols() assembling report (see next step) Conditions always read RAW column values — glued, cleared, deduped display text never changes rows match condition must TRUE/FALSE per row (one scalar); NA aborts create_report(), guard !.na(x) Multiple compute_cols() calls accumulate spec; actions combine arrival order, later actions win conflicting style properties value_from = NULL c_addrow() creates empty separator row detailed examples see Reporting Examples: Conditional Row Actions.
code: spec <- create_table(mtcars)  # Define a style for first group occurrences spec <- add_style(spec, id = "group_header", s_font(bold = TRUE, color = "#0000FF"))  # Apply style conditionally: highlight first occurrence of each cyl group spec <- compute_cols(spec, firstOf(cyl),    c_style(c(mpg, hp), styleRef = "group_header"))  # Add a separator row above first group spec <- compute_cols(spec, firstOf(cyl),    c_addrow(pos = "above")) # Direct column comparison (mtcars has no 'group'/'zebra' styles — # define every styleRef before referencing it; create_report() aborts # on undefined references) spec <- add_style(spec, id = "high_power", s_font(bold = TRUE)) compute_cols(spec, cyl > 6, c_style(mpg, styleRef = "high_power"))  # String matching (in a clinical listing, e.g.: Parameter == "Pulse") compute_cols(spec, am == 1, c_style(mpg, styleRef = "group_header"))  # Helper functions available INSIDE compute_cols() conditions: #   firstOf(col1, col2, ...)  — TRUE at the first row of each RUN of equal #                               values (contiguous groups — sort the data first) #   lastOf(col1, col2, ...)   — TRUE at the last row of each RUN #   firstRow()                — TRUE only for the very first data row #   lastRow()                 — TRUE only for the very last data row #   everyNth(n)               — TRUE every n-th row (1, n+1, 2n+1, ...) #   rowNumber()               — 1-based row index #   firstOfBlock(col, n, offset) — first row of every n-th block # Note: these helpers are NOT standalone functions — they only work inside # the condition argument of compute_cols().  compute_cols(spec, firstOf(cyl), c_style(c(mpg, hp), styleRef = "group_header")) compute_cols(spec, lastOf(cyl), c_addrow(pos = "below"))  # A scalar condition is allowed: compute_cols(spec, TRUE, ...) acts on all rows compute_cols(spec, TRUE, c_style(disp, styleRef = "group_header"))  # Combine conditions with base logical operators compute_cols(spec, cyl == 8 & hp > 100, c_style(mpg, styleRef = "high_power"))  # Aggregates are allowed as scalars: the condition below compares every row # against the whole-column mean (mean(cyl) > 4 evaluates once) compute_cols(spec, hp > mean(hp), c_style(hp, styleRef = "high_power"))

what: Option A: One step with write_doc() (recommended)
title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: write_doc() combines save + render single call: Additional parameters: toc: TRUE, prepends Word TOC field page. Entries come titles/subtitles carrying toclevel; none, field updates empty list. Default follows insertTOC option. tocTitle: heading TOC field (default "Table Contents"). prettify: TRUE, writes human-readable JSON metadata (useful debugging). DOCX bytes identical either way. verbose: TRUE, prints renderer progress messages R console. name passed without extension — write_doc() appends .docx, name = "demographics.docx" produce demographics.docx.docx. recommended approach production use. Set session defaults :
code: report <- create_report(spec_table, spec_text)  # Returns the full path to the generated .docx (invisibly) doc_path <- write_doc(report,   name     = "demographics",          # Output file name (no extension)   outDir   = "./output",              # Where the final .docx is written   metaPath = tempdir())               # Where JSON metadata is written (temp is fine) dir.create("./output", showWarnings = FALSE) dir.create("./meta", showWarnings = FALSE) tfl_set_options(   output_directory = "./output",   meta_directory   = "./meta" )  # Then write_doc() uses those defaults automatically write_doc(report, name = "demographics")

what: Option B: Two steps with save_report() + replay_report()
title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: Use need inspect version-control JSON metadata separately: save_report() output files: {metaPath}/{spec_hash}.json — main specification (consumed renderer) {metaPath}/{dataRef}.json — table data files (one per table spec) Figure files copied metaPath, original extension preserved
code: report <- create_report(spec_table, spec_text)  # Step 1: Serialize to JSON + data files result <- save_report(report,   docFileName = "my_report.docx",   outDir      = "./output",   metaPath    = tempdir(),   prettify    = TRUE)              # prettify = TRUE for readable JSON (debugging)  # Step 2: Re-render the DOCX from the saved JSON metadata replay_report(   spec_json   = result$spec_file,   meta_dir    = result$metaPath,   output_path = file.path("./output", "my_report.docx"))

previous_headings: Step 9: JSON metadata — what it is and why you might need it
title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: Every time write_doc() (save_report()) runs, writes intermediate files metaPath: {hash}.json — main spec file: document structure, column definitions, styles, titles, footnotes, headers/footers. C++ renderer reads. {dataRef}.json — One data file per table spec, containing actual row data. Figure files — Copied original paths metaPath. _index.json — index spec files written folder (auto-maintained). workflows, metaPath = tempdir() fine — care final .docx. real reasons use persistent metaPath.

text: Reproducibility / audit trail: regulated environments (FDA, EMA submissions), may need prove specific DOCX generated specific dataset specific time. spec JSON + data JSON together form complete, reproducible snapshot. Re-rendering stored metadata: JSON files exist, replay_report() re-renders DOCX straight — -memory specs data frames needed (still R call, needs nothing original session). Useful regenerating document template change, rendering different machine CI pipeline, reproducing output months later. Version management: save writes hash-named spec JSON; identical content reuses hash updates existing entry instead adding version. folder never prunes : replay_report("name.docx") always renders newest indexed version, clean_reports(keep_versions = 1) way trim history.

title: Getting Started with ksTFL
text: list_reports() returns data frame columns: doc_file, datetime, is_latest, n_specs, spec_file, data_refs. replay_report() re-renders JSON — R spec objects, data frames required. Pass either target .docx name (re-renders latest version) exact spec hash filename. clean_reports() removes obsolete JSON files. default keeps 1 version per document (keep_versions = 1). Always run dry_run = TRUE first.
code: meta_dir <- "./meta" # (report + ./meta set up by the previous chunks; write_doc already saved #  its spec there — or call save_report(report, "demo.docx", metaPath = meta_dir))  # List all spec JSONs in the meta folder df <- list_reports(meta_dir) print(df[df$is_latest, c("doc_file", "datetime", "spec_file")])  # Re-render a DOCX from stored JSON (no R objects needed) replay_report("demographics.docx", meta_dir = meta_dir)  # Or replay a specific version by its spec JSON file name some_spec <- df$spec_file[1] replay_report(some_spec, meta_dir = meta_dir,               output_path = "./output/demographics_v2.docx")  # Clean up obsolete spec files (keeps latest version per document) clean_reports(meta_dir, dry_run = TRUE)   # Preview what would be deleted clean_reports(meta_dir, dry_run = FALSE)  # Actually delete

what: Complete example: From data to document
title: Getting Started with ksTFL
code: library(ksTFL)  # --- Setup --- data <- data.frame(   subject = sprintf("S%03d", 1:10),   age = round(rnorm(10, 45, 10)),   sex = sample(c("M", "F"), 10, TRUE) )  # --- Create & customize --- spec <- create_table(data, cols = c(subject, age, sex))  spec <- add_style(spec, id = "header",                   s_font(bold = TRUE, font_size = "11pt"),                   s_paragraph(alignment = "center"),                   s_table_style(background_color = "#DDDDDD"))  spec <- define_cols(spec, c(subject, age, sex),                     label = c("Subject ID", "Age (years)", "Sex"),                     labelStyleRef = "header")  spec <- define_cols(spec, age, type = "numeric", format = "%.0f")  spec <- add_title(spec, "Demographics Table") spec <- add_subtitle(spec, "All subjects in safety population") spec <- add_footnote(spec, "Data are shown as observed.")  spec <- add_span_header(spec, c(age, sex), 'Characteristic',                          labelStyleRef = "header", stubOrder = 1) spec <- add_span_header(spec, c(subject, age, sex), 'Treatment A (N=10)',                          labelStyleRef = "header", stubOrder = 2)  spec <- set_document(spec, contentWidth = '40%')  # --- Export --- report <- create_report(spec) |>  write_doc('demographics')  # Done!

what: Example 1 — Demographics table with conditional formatting
title: Real Examples of Clinical Outputs using ksTFL
text: Demographics tables among common deliverables clinical reporting. summarise baseline patient characteristics treatment arm typically include section headers, summary statistics, inferential test results. example shows ksTFL handles declaratively. key techniques demonstrated : Invisible helper columns — SECTION, SECTION_ID, MODELVAL kept rendered document drive conditional logic via compute_cols(). core ksTFL pattern: data frame can carry metadata columns rendering engine never prints uses control formatting. c_addrow() — inserts bold section headers (Age, Sex, Race, Ethnicity) first row group, pulling text straight hidden SECTION column. c_merge() + c_glue() — p-value rows treatment columns merge one cell p-value appended, giving familiar centered p-value cell spanning arms (bare value, e.g. 0.041). Inline markup — <sup></sup> renders footnote reference marker population line, inside text passed add_title(). c_pageBreak() — forces break last section long tail table opens fresh page. Spacer rows — c_addrow("") row_h4 separates sections visually.

code: # --- Input data: a flat analyst frame, one row per statistic --- # Four parameter sections (Age, Sex, Race, Ethnicity); each ends with a # p-value row. Values are already in display form - the renderer never # re-formats what the analyst supplies. raw <- data.frame(   SECTION = c(rep("Age (years)", 6), rep("Sex", 3), rep("Race", 4),               rep("Ethnicity", 3)),   STAT = c("n", "Mean (SD)", "Median", "Q1; Q3", "Min; Max", "p-value (ANOVA)",            "Female", "Male", "p-value (Fisher)",            "White", "Asian", "Black or African American", "p-value (Fisher)",            "Hispanic or Latino", "Not Hispanic or Latino", "p-value (Fisher)"),   DRUGX = c("160", "55.2 (12.4)", "54.0", "47.0; 64.0", "18; 82", "",             "88 (55.0%)", "72 (45.0%)", "",             "130 (81.2%)", "18 (11.2%)", "12 (7.5%)", "",             "21 (13.1%)", "139 (86.9%)", ""),   PLCB  = c("158", "56.0 (11.9)", "55.0", "48.0; 63.0", "20; 81", "",             "90 (57.0%)", "68 (43.0%)", "",             "124 (78.5%)", "22 (13.9%)", "12 (7.6%)", "",             "18 (11.4%)", "140 (88.6%)", ""),   TOTAL = c("318", "55.6 (12.1)", "54.5", "47.5; 63.5", "18; 82", "",             "178 (56.0%)", "140 (44.0%)", "",             "254 (79.9%)", "40 (12.6%)", "24 (7.5%)", "",             "39 (12.3%)", "279 (87.7%)", ""), # MODELVAL is a hidden driver column: populated only on p-value rows, # NA everywhere else. compute_cols() below tests !is.na(MODELVAL) to # find exactly those rows - no extra flag column needed.   MODELVAL = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "0.041",                NA, NA, ">0.999",                NA, NA, NA, "0.772",                NA, NA, "0.664"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE) # Cumulative group index derived from first-seen order of SECTION. # It drives the spacer rows (lastOf) and the page break (== 4) below, # and is also hidden from the document. raw$SECTION_ID <- as.integer(cumsum(!duplicated(raw$SECTION))) SECTION                      STAT                    DRUGX         PLCB         TOTAL 1  Age (years)                  n                       160           158          318 2  Age (years)                  Mean (SD)               55.2 (12.4)   56.0 (11.9)  55.6 (12.1) 3  Age (years)                  Median                  54.0          55.0         54.5 4  Age (years)                  Q1; Q3                  47.0; 64.0    48.0; 63.0   47.5; 63.5 5  Age (years)                  Min; Max                18; 82        20; 81       18; 82 6  Age (years)                  p-value (ANOVA)                                     0.041 7  Sex                          Female                  88 (55.0%)    90 (57.0%)   178 (56.0%) 8  Sex                          Male                    72 (45.0%)    68 (43.0%)   140 (44.0%) 9  Sex                          p-value (Fisher)                                    >0.999 10 Race                         White                   130 (81.2%)   124 (78.5%)  254 (79.9%) 11 Race                         Asian                   18 (11.2%)    22 (13.9%)   40 (12.6%) 12 Race                         Black or African Am.    12 (7.5%)     12 (7.6%)    24 (7.5%) 13 Race                         p-value (Fisher)                                    0.772 14 Ethnicity                    Hispanic or Latino      21 (13.1%)    18 (11.4%)   39 (12.3%) 15 Ethnicity                    Not Hispanic or Latino  139 (86.9%)   140 (88.6%)  279 (87.7%) 16 Ethnicity                    p-value (Fisher)                                    0.664

code:
# --- Building the specification --- # create_table() takes the flat frame as-is; every presentation concern # is declared from here on, never baked into the data. spec <- create_table(raw) %>% # Multi-line title: table number on line 1, description on line 2. # toclevel = 1 tags the title for a Table of Contents (the TOC page is # written when write_doc(toc = TRUE) is used — see Example 4). add_title( c("Table S1", "Demographic and Baseline Characteristics"), toclevel = 1 ) %>% # Population line in italics. a is inline markup that the # renderer converts to real Word superscript - the footnote reference. add_title("Full Analysis Seta", styleRef = "font_italic") %>% # Footnote body; composition f_combine("fs_8", "fc_gray") assembles the # style from built-in atoms: 8-point font + gray color. add_footnote( paste0("a Values are shown as n (%), mean (SD), median, or quartiles; ", "percentages are based on the number of subjects in the treatment arm."), styleRef = f_combine("fs_8", "fc_gray") ) %>% # Hide the three helper columns. They are NOT printed, but stay visible # to all compute_cols() conditions - the core ksTFL metadata-column # pattern. define_cols(c(SECTION, SECTION_ID, MODELVAL), isVisible = FALSE) %>% # Stub column:
stacks the two label lines; labelStyleRef moves the # header text left, valueStyleRef indents every value one level so rows # sit visually under the bold section headers inserted later. define_cols(STAT, label = "Parameter
Statistic", labelStyleRef = "text_left", valueStyleRef = "indent_1" ) %>% # The three arms are defined in one batch with vectorised per-column # values (1-to-N mapping).
splits each header into name + (N=...); # the shared fixed width keeps the arms visually identical. define_cols(c(DRUGX, PLCB, TOTAL), label = c("DrugX
(N=160)", "Placebo
(N=158)", "Total
(N=318)"), valueStyleRef = "text_center", colWidth = "16%" ) %>% # 1. Section headers: on the FIRST row of every SECTION run insert a bold # row ABOVE it, pulling the text straight from the hidden SECTION # column - zero duplicated strings in the data. compute_cols( firstOf(SECTION), c_addrow("above", value_from = SECTION, styleRef = "font_bold") ) %>% # 2. p-value rows, three actions in one rule, evaluated left to right: # merge DrugX+Placebo into one centered italic cell with a thin top # border, italicise the statistic label, then glue the p-value text # after the merged cell - the centered "0.041" display. compute_cols( !is.na(MODELVAL), c_merge(c(DRUGX, PLCB), styleRef = f_combine("text_center", "bt_th", "i")), c_style(STAT, "i"), c_glue(DRUGX, "after", glue_col = MODELVAL) ) %>% # 3. Spacers: an empty 4-point row below each section gives the eye rest. # lastOf() is run-length-aware: it fires on the LAST row of each run. compute_cols( lastOf(SECTION_ID), c_addrow("below", styleRef = "row_h4") ) %>% # 4. Page break: the table is long, so the Ethnicity section (id 4) # deliberately starts on a fresh page instead of being split by Word. compute_cols( SECTION_ID == 4 & firstOf(SECTION_ID), c_pageBreak() ) %>% # Document-level polish: 75% content width centers the table as a # typographic choice; the zero empty lines remove the template's # default blank rows above and below the body. set_document( contentWidth = "75%", topEmptyLine = "0pt", bottomEmptyLine = "0pt" )

text: example uses default embedded style template. One ksTFL’s design principles content styling separate: can switch completely different visual theme changing single parameter already-built spec, without touching data conditional logic: table now wears Navy_Pro template — different fonts, colours, borders, identical content structure: Open example_01_navy.pdf Key take-aways example: Invisible columns — SECTION, SECTION_ID, MODELVAL never appear document, yet drive conditional logic. c_addrow(value_from = ...) pulls text hidden column inserted header row — manual string duplication. c_merge() + c_glue() combine cells append content another column one compute_cols() call. Inline <sup> markup carries footnote reference title. c_pageBreak() row_h4 spacers give precise control pagination whitespace. Template switching re-skins whole output via one option.
code: # One option swaps the entire corporate look: fonts, colors, borders # all come from the named template. Data and conditional logic are # untouched - styling is separable from content by design. spec <- set_document(spec, docTemplate = 'Navy_Pro') create_report(spec) %>% write_doc('example_01_navy')

title: Real Examples of Clinical Outputs using ksTFL
text: pipeline follows pattern Example 1: create table → titles/footnotes → hide helper columns → define visible columns → conditional row transforms → document settings. Reading inline comments alongside Example 1 help see one--one correspondence:
code:
# --- Build the specification object --- drg_N <- 16 plcb_N <- 17 total_N <- 33 spec_dm_01 <- create_table(data) %>% add_title( c("Таблица 1.2", "Демографические и другие исходные характеристики"), toclevel = 1 ) %>% add_title("Популяция FAS", styleRef = 'font_italic') %>% add_footnote('Источник: Перечень 16.3; Перечень 16.33') %>% # The CAT1 variable holds the category name. We want those # names to appear in the CAT2 column as section headers, # so we hide CAT1. We also hide the helper columns SECTORD1 # and modelval (whose values we place into other cells): define_cols(c(CAT1, SECTORD1, modelval), isVisible = F) %>% # First value of each CAT1 group becomes an extra header row: compute_cols( # built-in helper: first value within a group # (can also define composite groups from several variables) firstOf(CAT1), # Insert a bold row above with the value from CAT1 c_addrow('above', value_from = CAT1, styleRef = 'font_bold') ) %>% ## Indent CAT2 values to the right relative to the header. ## This can be done in two ways... # Method 1: via a per-row rule: # compute_cols(!is.na(CAT2), c_style(CAT2, 'indent_1')) # Method 2: by setting the column style directly. # Method 2 is preferable here because we apply the same # style to every value in the column; doing it per-row via # compute_cols creates unnecessary rendering overhead. # We also define the column label and header style: define_cols(CAT2, label = 'Параметр
Статистика', valueStyleRef = 'indent_1', labelStyleRef = 'text_left') %>% # Labels for the remaining treatment-arm columns: define_cols(c(RPH104, PLCB, TOTAL), label = c( paste0('Drug-001', '
(N=', drg_N, ')'), paste0('Плацебо', '
(N=', plcb_N, ')'), paste0('Всего', '
(N=', total_N, ')') ), # center arms; the everything() pass below layers 8 pt on # top of these styles without touching alignment valueStyleRef = 'text_center', colWidth = '15%' ) %>% define_cols(everything(), valueStyleRef = 'fs_8') %>% # Display modelval in a merged cell spanning RPH104 + PLCB: compute_cols( !is.na(modelval), # Merge cells; centre the value and draw a thin top border # to show it relates to both treatment columns: c_merge(c(RPH104, PLCB), styleRef = f_combine('text_center', 'bt_th', 'i')), c_style(CAT2, 'i'), # Append modelval into the merged cell c_glue(RPH104, 'after', glue_col = modelval) ) %>% # Separators between groups compute_cols( lastOf(SECTORD1), c_addrow('below', styleRef = 'row_h4') ) %>% # Manual page break: first 3 categories on page one, # the rest on page two: compute_cols( SECTORD1 == 4 & firstOf(SECTORD1), c_pageBreak() ) %>% set_document( contentWidth = '75%', # Place footnotes in the document footer section footnotePlace = 'doc_footer', # Use an alternative embedded template docTemplate = 'Classic_landscape_times' ) create_report(spec_dm_01) %>% write_doc("example_02_demog")

title: Real Examples of Clinical Outputs using ksTFL
text: Adverse Event (AE) frequency tables staple clinical safety reporting. often many columns (treatment periods, follow-windows, overall totals) arranged multi-level spanning headers. example demonstrates: Three-tier spanning headers via add_span_header() stubOrder stack period sub-headers, follow-banner, top-level drug-arm header. Custom page layout — landscape A4 tight margins fit 14 numeric columns plus two identifier columns. isID = TRUE — marks columns repeat every page table spans multiple pages. Conditional formatting — bold SOC-level totals, inserted header rows per System Organ Class, forced page break “AE” summary per-SOC detail.
